title: The Shadow Hand
next_chapter_hook: At the end of that secret letter, an ancient seal Chen Ji had never seen before was unmistakably stamped—the private seal of his father Chen Xuan. Beneath the seal, a line of text made his pupils shrink sharply: 'My son, if you are reading this letter, it means Zhang Shen has already made his move.'

text.content:
The night was as dark as ink. Chen Ji's footsteps never stopped, yet his heart remained as clear as a mirror.

That faint, ethereal presence hid in the shadows at the corner, almost imperceptible—had he not repeatedly divined his surroundings these past days using the Tianji Record, he would have nearly missed it. That gaze was cold and familiar, like a venomous snake lurking in the darkness, ready to strike at any moment.

He didn't look back, didn't quicken his pace. He merely drew his right hand slightly into his sleeve, fingertips quietly touching that cold copper coin—the transformed remnant of the Tianji Record.

'They came rather quickly.' A faint smile curved his lips, his voice low enough for only himself to hear.

dialogue.content: (Self-mocking whisper) Su Qingyao just left, and these people couldn't wait to show themselves. Truly... thought-provoking.

text.content:
Chen Ji deliberately slowed his pace, turning into a secluded alley. High walls lined both sides, their tops covered with withered vines. The moonlight was thin, barely illuminating the stones beneath his feet.

The presence behind him indeed followed.

Chen Ji leaned against the corner, holding his breath and focusing his mind. His perception spread through the darkness, capturing the other person's aura—not high in cultivation, roughly late Qi Refining stage. Their steps were unsteady, clearly not skilled at direct confrontation.

This type was best suited for scouting, for espionage.

He quickly sketched a name in his mind: a registered disciple under Zhang Shen, one of the more cunning servants among the Outer Disciples—Zhao Si.

Zhang Shen. Outer Sect Elder of the Tianqing Sect, in charge of dispatching and examining Servant Disciples. The man appeared amicable on the surface, smiling at everyone he met, yet his heart was narrow and petty. He delighted most in sabotaging people behind their backs.

Chen Ji had no direct conflict with this man, but he remembered clearly—when his father Chen Xuan was still in the sect, Zhang Shen had attempted multiple times to become his disciple, only to be refused each time.

How long would a rejected person hold a grudge?

A cold smile curled Chen Ji's lips. He drew a dark golden talisman from his sleeve, pressing it lightly against the corner of the wall. Tracking Talisman—a secret technique recorded in the Tianji Record Fragment, especially sensitive to tracing auras.

choice.prompt: The Tracking Talisman has been set. Chen Ji must choose in the shadows—to directly track this lackey to investigate the mastermind behind, or does he have other plans?

choices.text: Follow in Shadow, Discover the Truth
choices.description: Following the Tracking Talisman's guidance, quietly follow Zhao Si to see who he meets, thoroughly uncovering this hidden line.
choices.risk_hint: If Discovered, Identity May Be Exposed

text.content:
Chen Ji's figure flickered, silently gliding onto the wall top. Stepping on the withered vines for leverage, his entire body slid along the eaves like a shadow. The Tracking Talisman at the corner of the wall radiated faint warmth, emitting a subtle spiritual light only he could perceive, guiding the direction of Zhao Si's path.

That fellow indeed didn't return directly to his quarters. He took multiple turns, finally stopping before a secluded courtyard—the residence adjacent to Outer Sect Elder Zhang Shen's dwelling, a side courtyard ordinarily used to store miscellaneous items.

choices.description: Deliberately reveal a weakness, lure Zhao Si into the trap. Let him believe he has caught Chen Ji's把柄, then follow the vine to揪出 the mastermind behind.
choices.visible_reward: Let the Enemy Walk Into the Net
choices.risk_hint: If the Foe is Cunning, May See Through It

text.content:
Chen Ji didn't continue following. Instead, he silently doubled back to his own quarters. He retrieved a prepared 'prop' from his chest—a forged letter, its handwriting an imitation of his father Chen Xuan's script from when he was alive, containing some ambiguous 'last words.'

He would let Zhao Si 'accidentally' discover this letter, letting him believe he had found Chen Ji's weakness.

What would a greedy villain do upon discovering a tremendous secret?

The answer was self-evident.

Chen Ji chose the first path.

In the night, his form moved like a specter through eaves and shadows, always maintaining the precise distance from Zhao Si—close enough not to be shaken off, far enough not to arouse suspicion.

Zhao Si stopped before that side courtyard, looked around, then knocked on the courtyard door. Three short, one long—that was the signal.

A moment later, the courtyard door silently cracked open. An old, gloomy voice drifted out: 'Come in.'

Chen Ji held his breath, hiding his form within the shadows at the corner of the wall. He saw Zhao Si duck inside with servile haste, a sliver of dim lamplight leaking through the door gap.

dialogue.content: (Inner cold laugh) Three short, one long—how methodical. Old dog Zhang Shen trains his dogs with signals too. Pity... a dog is still a dog. No matter how it barks, its fate is only to bite on its master's behalf.

text.content:
Chen Ji silently pressed against the courtyard wall, fingertips resting on the bricks. The Tracking Talisman's residual warmth remained; following that faint connection, he captured the exchange of voices drifting from the courtyard.

'...What has that废物 been up to these past days?'

The aged voice belonged to Zhang Shen. Chen Ji's pupils narrowed—the old dog couldn't hold still after all.

'Reporting to Elder, that Chen Ji has been keeping a low profile these days. Other than borrowing some worthless功法 fragments from the scripture pavilion, nothing unusual.' Zhao Si's voice carried sycophancy. 'In this one's view, he truly is just a废物—utterly no threat.'

'Waste?' Zhang Shen coldly laughed. 'Do you not know what kind of figure Chen Xuan was back then? A son of such a man—how could he possibly be a废物!'

Chen Ji's fist secretly clenched within his sleeve.

Father Chen Xuan—what exactly happened back then? Why did everyone speak that name with such taboo-laden wariness?

He continued listening.

'Elder, rest assured. This one has already turned Chen Xuan's old effects inside out as you instructed.' Zhao Si lowered his voice. 'It's just... those things were all sealed by the sect. This one dares not act carelessly.'

'Idiot!' Zhang Shen cursed in a low voice. 'I told you to search for Chen Xuan's hand-written notes, diaries, letters! Those are what matter!'

'Yes, yes, this one understands. But that Chen Ji seems wary too. These past days of following him, this one feels he might suspect something...'

choice.prompt: Having overheard Zhang Shen's key intelligence and plans, Chen Ji must decide his next move.

choices.text: Continue to Hide, Gather More Evidence
choices.description: Keep steady, continue eavesdropping. Strive to fully grasp Zhang Shen's entire scheme before seeking an opportunity to net them all.

text.content:
Chen Ji suppressed the fury in his heart, continuing to listen.

Zhang Shen's voice grew increasingly sinister: 'Chen Xuan discovered something extraordinary back then—something足以让整个天青宗改天换地. Sect Master Ling Yuan appears to have sealed Chen Xuan's remains on the surface, but in truth... Hmph, he wants to find those things more than anyone.'

'Does Elder mean...' Zhao Si probed.

'What I mean is, Ling Yuan is waiting like an old fox. And I—no longer wish to wait.' Zhang Shen's voice carried ruthless determination. 'Watch that废物 closely. If he shows any unusual movement, report to me immediately. If you can find what Chen Xuan left behind, we share the spoils.'

choices.description: Deliberately expose your presence. Drive Zhang Shen into panic, see what overreaching moves he makes next—instead, you can grasp his把柄.
choices.visible_reward: Let the Enemy Make the First Mistake
choices.risk_hint: Zhang Shen May Desperately Take Action

text.content:
Chen Ji lightly flicked his fingers. A Tracking Talisman transformed into flowing light, vanishing into the night sky. The next moment, the lanterns in the courtyard wavered violently. Zhang Shen's voice cut off abruptly.

'Who goes there!'

A faint smile curved Chen Ji's lips. His form flickered, vanishing into the darkness. He didn't engage in battle—there was no need to. He merely needed Zhang Shen to know that someone was watching him from the shadows.

A guilty person, facing unknown surveillance—what would they do?

The answer was more useful than anything he could say himself.

Chen Ji chose to continue hiding.

He had an intuition—the words Zhang Shen was about to say next held the real key.

As expected, after a brief silence, Zhang Shen's voice rang out again, carrying an irrepressible greed: 'Back then, Chen Xuan discovered the trail of the Tianji Record. He wanted to claim that thing for himself alone—and so he was...'

'Was killed by whom?' Zhao Si couldn't help but ask.

'Silence!' Zhang Shen sharply cut him off. 'There are some things you shouldn't ask.'

After a stretch of silence, Zhang Shen's voice returned, tinged with gloom: 'In any case, since that废物 has returned to the Tianqing Sect, he is a key delivered to our doorstep. His blood carries Chen Xuan's lineage—and Chen Xuan's blood can open that lock.'

dialogue.content: (Inner shock) My blood... can open that lock? Father, what did you leave behind? Why does everyone want to obtain it?

text.content:
Chen Ji's nails dug deeply into his palms, blood seeping between his fingers.

He finally understood.

His father's death was no accident.

Those elders who had seemed to care for him daily, those smiling masters who said 'accept your condolences'—among them, someone had personally pushed his father into the abyss.

And now, their gazes have turned to him.

Not because he was Chen Xuan's son, not because he was a disciple of the Tianqing Sect, but because he was a 'key.'

A key that could open some forbidden door.

choice.prompt: After learning the truth, Chen Ji faces a choice—follow the original plan and act slowly, or take direct action while momentum favors him tonight?

choices.text: Bear It in Silence, Set Up in Shadow
choices.description: Bury tonight's gains deep in your heart. Quietly gather more evidence, wait until the timing matures, then take them all down at once.

text.content:
Chen Ji took a deep breath, pressing the inferno of rage into the deepest recesses of his heart.

Anger was the most useless thing. It only made people lose reason, made them expose weaknesses.

He silently withdrew from beyond the courtyard wall, vanishing into the night.

Zhang Shen, Zhao Si, and those as-yet-unseen masterminds—he inscribed their names one by one into his heart.

Someday, he would let them know what it meant to 'plan without any oversight.'

choices.description: Since Zhang Shen wants to use him as a key, let this key become a blade thrust back at him—turn the tables, make the enemy suffer their own schemes.
choices.risk_hint: If Seen Through, Will Fall Into Desperate Straits

text.content:
A cold light flickered in Chen Ji's eyes as a faint smile curved his lips.

Zhang Shen wants to use his blood as a key?

Then let him come test which door this key will open.

The door to heaven, or the door to hell.

He turned and left, footsteps silent, yet in his heart a bold plan had already formed—one sufficient to bring Zhang Shen to utter ruin.

Returning to his quarters, Chen Ji did not immediately rest.

He retrieved a dust-covered wooden box from beneath his bed—the wooden box was one of the remains left by his father Chen Xuan. He had gone through it countless times before. Beyond a few yellowed hand-written notes and some indecipherable talisman diagrams, he had found nothing special.

But tonight, he decided to search once more, more carefully.

Zhang Shen said his father discovered the trail of the Tianji Record. And the Tianji Record... was precisely his greatest reliance now.

Was there some connection between the two?

Chen Ji took out each item from the wooden box, spreading them on the table.

Twelve volumes of hand-written notes, seven talisman diagrams, a jade pendant that had already lost its spiritual nature, and... a piece of paper folded neatly.

His movements abruptly stopped.

This piece of paper—he had never seen it before.

Or rather, he had seen it before, but never paid it any mind—because it was too unremarkable. Just an ordinary yellow paper, tucked between the diagrams, as if used as a makeshift page marker.

But tonight, his state of mind was different.

He carefully unfolded that piece of paper. The handwriting that met his eyes made his pupils shrink sharply—it was his father's script, the handwriting he knew so intimately.

'For my son Chen Ji—'

dialogue.content: (Inner shock, voice trembling) Father... did you foresee this day long ago?

text.content:
Chen Ji's fingers trembled slightly. He forced himself to remain calm, continuing to read.

'If you are reading this letter, it means Zhang Shen has already made his move.'

'When I discovered the Tianji Record, I knew this thing was ill-fated. It can foresee heavenly secrets, but it will certainly be counteracted by heavenly fate. Every holder throughout history met a bad end.'

'I concealed the Tianji Record Fragment within your body, originally intending to tell you the truth when your cultivation was sufficient. Who would have thought fate would play such a cruel trick—I ultimately did not get to wait for that day.'

'Ji'er, Zhang Shen is merely a chess piece. The true chess player is someone else. That person... is Ling Yuan.'

Chen Ji's breath abruptly quickened.

Ling Yuan. The former Sect Master of the Tianqing Sect. The old senior who had 'grief-strickenly' presided over the funeral after his father's death, who had 'caringly' received him when he returned to the sect—

was actually the true mastermind behind his father's murder?

He continued reading, his heart pounding faster and faster.

'I once saw a vision in the Tianji Record—you and Ling Yuan will ultimately have one decisive battle. The outcome of that battle, I cannot see. But I believe in you.'

'One final matter: if you one day behold the Eye of Heavenly Dao, always remember—'

'It is not your enemy.'

'It is the existence you must surpass.'

The letter ended abruptly, as if something unpredictable had occurred while his father wrote this final line.

dialogue.content: (A desolate and transcendent voice suddenly rings in Chen Ji's ear) Chen Xuan's son, you have finally begun to touch the truth. But remember—the more you know, the closer you draw to fate's end.

text.content:
Chen Ji abruptly lifted his head, scanning in all directions.

The room was empty, yet that voice was so clear, as if sounding directly in the depths of his mind.

The Eye of Heavenly Dao.

It... was watching him.
